parts.note: a philatelic term for an envelope, read instead as the covering Adam and Eve wore at the very beginning of creation

explanation.surface: A stamp collector's envelope postmarked on the day of issue.
explanation.walkthrough: A first-day cover is a stamp collector's item, but read literally it is the covering worn on the first days of humanity in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve covered themselves with leaves of the fig tree in Genesis, the earliest clothing.

parts.note: foot soldiers are infantry
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Film shot of soldiers from a period of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film material.

clue.text: Garden flower to die out in Georgia

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: out shows the letters of to die are put out of order

explanation.surface: A flower dying out in the state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles TO DIE; 'in' puts the result within the state abbreviation. 'die out' reads as one phrase but splits between fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Godetia is an annual plant with showy blooms, grown in beds.

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words Essex tolerated

explanation.surface: Asking whether people in Essex put up with a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it highly.

clue.text: If upside down, fit another hearth

indicators.note: in a down clue upside down means the word If is read upwards

parts.note: to replace is to fit another in place of the old

explanation.surface: Fitting a new hearth if the old one is overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the floor of the grate where the fire burns.

clue.text: Cats, for example, can be so melodious

explanation.surface: A remark that the show Cats can be really tuneful.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats is a stage show with songs, a genre piece; and tuneful sounds are pleasing to the ear.

parts.note: mum means silent
PS is the abbreviation for private secretary

explanation.surface: A quiet personal assistant has a swollen gland.
explanation.definitionFit: Parotitis is inflammation of the salivary glands, the viral childhood illness.

clue.text: Good job one stands upright in a fiddle

definitions.text: one stands upright in a fiddle

parts.note: sound means good or reliable
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A good job with someone upright involved in a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wooden peg wedged upright between the belly and back of a violin.

parts.note: a cell is a cramped hole, as in a prison
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sculptor scoring a hole in one at golf.
explanation.walkthrough: Benvenuto Cellini was a Renaissance Italian sculptor and goldsmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Benvenuto Cellini was a Florentine goldsmith and maker of bronze statues.

indicators.note: break out means the letters of let nine escape into a new order

explanation.surface: A merciful jailer lets nine prisoners escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means merciful, gentle in judgement.

clue.text: One getting on sold out to better half

indicators.note: sold out suggests the letters of sold being knocked out of order
better half points to the back half of the word better, not a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone elderly sold out to their spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SOLD to OLDS; 'half' takes TER, the second half of 'better'. 'Better half' looks like a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is an elderly person, an old-timer.

clue.text: Mawkish girl, called into garden, gets nothing in return

parts.note: Tennyson's poem has the line Come into the garden, Maud, so the girl is Maud

indicators.note: in return shows the word for nothing is turned backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A sentimental girl is summoned into the garden and gets nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns NIL into LIN. The famous line 'Come into the garden, Maud' (Tennyson, also a Victorian parlour song) names the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully sentimental, which is what mawkish describes.

clue.text: Opens late, perhaps, for these graceful jumpers

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the phrase Opens late is one possible arrangement of other letters

explanation.surface: Musing about a shop that opens late and its leaping animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of OPENS LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: These animals are fleet deer-like grazers famed for springing leaps.

clue.text: Steer car right into sleazy bar

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable drinking place

explanation.surface: Guiding a car straight into a seedy bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide a motor vehicle along is to operate it on the road.

parts.note: land means a country

explanation.surface: Something located in a country to the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer to 11-across, a family of graceful jumping animals; this is a large African member of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is the largest African species of that horned grazing family.

clue.text: Where canvassers stand, with heavy rounds?

explanation.surface: Election workers standing about with thick sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvassers call at front entrances of houses; and very thick slices of bread are jokingly given this name.

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: Someone who defends a point in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who argues in support of a cause or belief speaks up for it.

clue.text: Dismissed, better equipped to be a haberdasher

parts.note: out means dismissed, as a batsman in cricket
fitter means more suitable or better equipped

explanation.surface: A sacked shopkeeper better kitted out for the trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of men's clothes and accessories.

indicators.note: bad implies the letters of hedonists are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers described as wicked and dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt people are deceitful and untrustworthy, lacking honesty.

clue.text: Do speed that is reckless-get sent down!

indicators.note: reckless means the letters of Do speed are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: Drive recklessly fast and you will end up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reckless' rearranges DO SPEED. 'Sent down' looks like jailed, but here it means removed from power.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ousted from office has been brought down from a throne or position.

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: An angry girl who will become fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the noun: the diagonal cross of St Andrew on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-shaped heraldic cross, as on the Scottish flag.

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are borne within the words conspirator chap

explanation.surface: A firebrand held by a plotting man, like Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a burning piece of wood used as a light.

clue.text: Affair of upright type at church

parts.note: roman is upright typeface, as opposed to italic
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: An affair with an upstanding sort at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A love relationship, especially a brief one, is a romantic liaison.

indicators.note: off means the letters of head and Yes are set awry

explanation.surface: An excited affirmation that an American bumpkin has lost his head.
explanation.definitionFit: US slang for a country bumpkin, a rustic.

explanation.surface: Rail termini used by some travellers from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The ends of an axis or magnet are its extremities; and people from Poland are Europeans.

parts.note: thin means emaciated
gummy means having no teeth, showing only gums

explanation.surface: Asking the name of a gaunt man with no teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A placeholder word for someone whose name you cannot remember, like whatsit or so-and-so.

clue.text: Royal house sending back staff to Utah

indicators.note: sending back means the whole run of staff to Utah is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a staff
UT is the abbreviation for the US state of Utah

explanation.surface: A royal family returning its employees to Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending back' reverses ROD+UT as one run, giving TUDOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The dynasty of Henry VII, Henry VIII and Elizabeth I ruled England 1485-1603.

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of a drug are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Keeping watch over an outfit running drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a sentry or lookout on duty.

clue.text: In the pay of the beak, gratuity is included in dispatch

indicators.note: is included in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: send means dispatch
a tip is a gratuity

explanation.surface: A bribe tucked into a parcel for a corrupt magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beak' is British slang for a magistrate (or headmaster); a stipendiary magistrate is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed salary, especially for a clergyman or salaried magistrate.

indicators.note: casualty suggests Aintree being wrecked into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A fallen rider at Aintree, maybe an inexperienced one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casualty' rearranges AINTREE, the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National is run.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner in training is a beginner.

clue.text: Actor's assistant with his back to the wall?

definitions.text: with his back to the wall?

explanation.surface: An actor's helper standing against the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre helper who looks after costumes; and a kitchen sideboard placed against a wall.

indicators.note: rotting means the letters of here and Dad decay into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad complains of carrots going rotten here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotting' rearranges HERE and DAD together. 'Carrots' is a nickname for a ginger-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots is a teasing nickname for someone with ginger hair.
